title: Frobenius compatibility with tower transitions

proof.text:
Put $G=L(g')^*$, $J=Rf'_*$, $s=G(r):E_m\to E_n$ and $\kappa'_i=\kappa_{g',K_i}$. The functor isomorphism $\kappa_{g'}$ has naturality equation $G\Phi_X(r)\kappa'_m=\kappa'_n\Phi_{X'}(s)$. Thus the induced Weil structures satisfy
$$
s\vartheta_{E,m}=G(r\vartheta_m)\kappa'_m
=G(\vartheta_n)G\Phi_X(r)\kappa'_m
=\vartheta_{E,n}\Phi_{X'}(s).
$$
By the finite-level exchange restriction lemma, $\gamma_i=\beta_{f',E_i}$ is the restricted ambient exchange, and its coefficient-change identification is natural; hence $J\Phi_{X'}(s)\gamma_m=\gamma_n\Phi_{Y'}(Js)$. Since $d_{m,n}=Js$, the defining composite for D yields
$$
\begin{aligned}
d_{m,n}\Theta_{D,m}
&=J(s\vartheta_{E,m})\gamma_m\\
&=J(\vartheta_{E,n})J\Phi_{X'}(s)\gamma_m\\
&=J(\vartheta_{E,n})\gamma_n\Phi_{Y'}(Js)
=\Theta_{D,n}\Phi_{Y'}(d_{m,n}).
\end{aligned}
$$

Write $a=a_{m,n}$, $b=b_{m,n}$ and $\Phi=\Phi_{Y'}$. The transition lemma gives $bh_m=h_na$ and hence $ah_m^{-1}=h_n^{-1}b$. By the transport definition and step 1,
$$
\begin{aligned}
a\Theta_{A,m}
&=h_n^{-1}b\Theta_{B,m}\Phi(h_m)\\
&=h_n^{-1}\Theta_{B,n}\Phi(b)\Phi(h_m)\\
&=h_n^{-1}\Theta_{B,n}\Phi(h_n)\Phi(a)
=\Theta_{A,n}\Phi(a).
\end{aligned}
$$
Only associativity, functoriality and the inverse identities for the displayed isomorphisms are used in this calculation.

Write $c=c_{m,n}$, $d=d_{m,n}$ and $\Phi=\Phi_{Y'}$. The transition lemma gives $dh'_m=h'_nc$, whence $c(h'_m)^{-1}=(h'_n)^{-1}d$. Using step 2 gives
$$
\begin{aligned}
c\Theta_{C,m}
&=(h'_n)^{-1}d\Theta_{D,m}\Phi(h'_m)\\
&=(h'_n)^{-1}\Theta_{D,n}\Phi(d)\Phi(h'_m)\\
&=(h'_n)^{-1}\Theta_{D,n}\Phi(h'_n)\Phi(c)
=\Theta_{C,n}\Phi(c).
\end{aligned}
$$
For each corner Z the proved equation $z_{m,n}\Theta_{Z,m}=\Theta_{Z,n}\Phi(z_{m,n})$ is exactly the condition that the family $\Theta_{Z,i}:\Phi Z_i\to Z_i$ be a tower map. The transition lemma states the four tower-map equations for $h,h',v,v'$. The finite Weil rectangle states, for each of these edges $e:Z\to W$, $e_i\Theta_{Z,i}=\Theta_{W,i}\Phi(e_i)$. Therefore each edge is a tower map whose components are Weil-equivariant, which is the asserted morphism of Weil towers. Compatibility for nonadjacent levels follows by composing the adjacent equations and using functoriality; the identity transition equation is immediate.
